options.label: keep the CA-MTL-3 network volume
options.storage_basis: the 100 GB volume at $0.24/day, idle or not
options.boot_basis: 278.9 s off the volume, every pass
options.risk: the volume pins the datacenter. SPEC 3.11 (1)'s capacity clause makes the GPU CLASS the contract and the datacenter a convenience — and on 2026-08-06 an A6000 stock-out in CA-MTL-3 blocked the run while the volume kept billing.

options.label: delete it, re-stage the 59 GB per pass onto pod NVMe
options.storage_basis: no volume, and a running pod's container disk is inside its hourly rate
options.boot_basis: 240 s staging + 46.229 s cold start (the faster cold start, after the download that buys it)
options.risk: every pass depends on the download completing; ~4 min is one measurement, not a distribution. In exchange there is no datacenter pin: A6000 in any region.

options.label: stopped pod with the weights on its container disk
options.storage_basis: ~80 GB of container disk billing while stopped, about what the 100 GB volume costs per month (knowledge/hot.md) — an approximation, not a posted price
options.boot_basis: 46.229 s, the weights are already on local disk
options.risk: resume is NOT guaranteed. The capacity clause pins the GPU class, never one pod, and a stopped pod's host can be reclaimed; `runpodctl pod list` shows running pods only, so an unavailable one does not announce itself.

common_to_all_options.note: the inference compute itself. It is the same in all three options, and its size is an ASSUMPTION here — 758 rows is test v4's count, and what a production pass actually carries is what 5c2 prices off this phase's collection.

recommendation: RECOMMENDATION: (b) delete it, re-stage the 59 GB per pass onto pod NVMe — $2.53/mo against $9.66 for keeping the volume, $7.14/mo saved, and the boot it costs (286 s) is within 7 s of what the volume already charges for. The saving is the smaller half of the argument: deleting the volume also removes the datacenter pin that blocked 5b, which is the failure this project has actually had. The DECISION is the operator's at acceptance.
decision: OPEN — the volume's fate is the operator's at acceptance. SPEC §3.11 (6) says this calculation advances the ~2026-09-05 review; it does not take it.
